question: Can an LLM act as an optimizer, generating new solutions from a prompt containing past solutions and their scores, and does this find better task prompts than human-written ones?
hypothesis: An LLM shown the optimization trajectory (solutions with scores) in a meta-prompt can iteratively propose better solutions, including better instructions for a scorer LLM.
contributions: Propose OPRO, optimization by prompting, with a meta-prompt of solution-score pairs and a task description
Show it on linear regression and TSP
Apply it to prompt optimization on GSM8K and BBH, beating human-designed prompts
Show optimized prompts transfer to MultiArith and AQuA

method.summary: At each step an optimizer LLM receives a meta-prompt with the best 20 prior solutions and scores (ascending order) plus task exemplars, and is sampled 8 times; the new solutions are scored and added. For prompt optimization the score is accuracy of a scorer LLM using the generated instruction on a training subset.
method.task: LLM-driven black-box optimization; prompt (instruction) optimization for reasoning tasks

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: 3.5% of train sampled (fixed subset) for optimization; full test set for evaluation

datasets.name: BIG-Bench Hard (23 tasks)
datasets.split: 20% of each task for optimization, remaining 80% test

datasets.name: Synthetic linear regression
datasets.size: 50 points, x from 1 to 50, standard Gaussian noise

inference.decoding: scorer: greedy (temperature 0) when evaluating instructions; optimizer: sampled
inference.temperature: 1.0 default for optimizer; 0 for scorer; ablation 0.0 to 2.0 (Fig 10)
inference.samples: 8 instructions per step, 200 steps default; ablation results are mean of 3 optimization repetitions; linear regression 5 runs; TSP 5 instances per n
inference.prompting: Meta-prompt: past instructions with scores sorted ascending, 3 random training exemplars, meta-instructions; scorer instruction position Q_begin, Q_end or A_begin

parameters.score_presentation: accuracy rounded to integer (100 buckets); ablation 20 buckets or none
parameters.linear_regression: 5 random start pairs, best 20 pairs, 8 candidates per step, temperature 1.0
parameters.TSP: 5 random start solutions, at most 8 new solutions per step

other.scorer_pairing: pre-trained PaLM 2-L scorer uses A_begin; text-bison uses Q_begin or Q_end
other.initial_instruction_default: empty string for text-bison; empty (BBH) or 'Let's solve the problem.' (GSM8K) for PaLM 2-L
other.ablation_setup: text-bison scorer, PaLM 2-L optimizer; GSM8K and BBH sports_understanding
other.no_validation_set: default setting sets aside no validation set

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of correct answers on train subset (objective) and held-out test set

metrics.name: optimality gap (TSP)
metrics.definition: (distance of solution minus oracle distance) divided by oracle distance

metrics.name: steps / unique pairs to optimum (linear regression)
metrics.definition: steps and unique (w,b) pairs explored before reaching global optimum

baselines: 'Let's think step by step.' (Kojima et al., 2022)
'Let's work this out in a step by step way to be sure we have the right answer.' (Zhou et al., 2022b)
EvoPrompt GA and DE (Guo et al., 2023)
eval.protocol: Instruction chosen by training accuracy in the default setting; Table 4 reports the instruction with highest test accuracy per scorer-optimizer pair. Single optimization run for main tables (repetition counts stated only for ablations and linear regression).

prompts.text:
I have some texts along with their corresponding scores. The texts are arranged in ascending order based on their scores, where higher scores indicate better quality.
text:
Let’s figure it out!
score:
61
text:
Let’s solve the problem.
score:
63
(. . . more instructions and scores ...)
The following exemplars show how to apply your text: you replace <INS> in each input with your text, then read the input and give an output. We say your output is wrong if your output is different from the given output, and we say your output is correct if they are the same.
input:
Q: ... A: <INS>
output:
140
(. . . more exemplars ...)
Write your new text that is different from the old ones and has a score as high as possible. Write the text in square brackets.

prompts.purpose: Meta-prompt for GPT models on GSM8K (Figure 22)
prompts.text:
Your task is to generate the instruction <INS>. Below are some previous instructions with their scores. The score ranges from 0 to 100.
... Generate an instruction that is different from all the instructions <INS> above, and has a higher score than all the instructions <INS> above. The instruction should begin with <INS> and end with </INS>. The instruction should be concise, effective, and generally applicable to all problems above.

prompts.purpose: Meta-prompt for pre-trained PaLM 2-L on GSM8K (Figure 21)
prompts.text:
Create a piece of text at the beginning of the answer to enhance the precision in solving diverse grade school math problems.
Precision: 4 <TEXT>A dime</TEXT>
...

Now you will help me minimize a function with two input variables w, b. ... Give me a new (w, b) pair that is different from all pairs above, and has a function value lower than any of the above. Do not write code. The output must end with a pair [w, b], where w and b are numerical values.

limits: Authors: OPRO is not meant to beat gradient-based optimizers or specialized TSP solvers; context length limits problem size (Sec 3.2 Limitations).
Authors: farthest insertion beats all LLMs on TSP as n grows; OPRO degrades quickly with larger n.
Authors: optimizer does not effectively use error cases; including them gave similar results.
Authors: prompt optimization needs a training set (at least tens of samples) and overfits; train accuracy often 5-20% above test.
Authors: sensitive to initialization; weaker start points converge slower (Fig 9b).
Main results are single runs on PaLM 2 / text-bison / GPT-3.5 / GPT-4 of 2023; best-instruction picks in Table 4 are by test accuracy.
Optimized instructions are model-specific; no human or statistical significance test reported for main tables.
Failure cases (Appendix A): hallucinated function values, repeating earlier solutions, getting stuck on the Rosenbrock function.

terms.definition: The prompt to the LLM serves as a call to the optimizer, and we name it the meta-prompt.
We denote the LLM for objective function evaluation as the scorer LLM, and the LLM for optimization as the optimizer LLM.
Instruction placed before the question, after the question, or at the beginning of the scorer output.
